No yellow precipitate, so Pb2+ likely absent.

Test for Zn2+ using NaOH? Already did NH3, but Zn(OH)2 would dissolve. Not present.

Test for Cu2+ using NH3 gives deep blue solution; not present.

Thus likely cation(s) are Mn2+ (black precipitate of Mn(OH)2 turning black) or Fe3+ (but Fe gave red complex). So Mn2+ seems plausible.

We can test for Mn2+ using addition of H2O2 and NaOH to produce brown MnO2 precipitate? Not available. Could use addition of KOH then H2O2? Not.

Alternatively test for Mn2+ using addition of NaOH then H2O2 yields brown precipitate; but we already have black precipitate.

Maybe also Al3+ gives white precipitate, not black.

Thus likely only Mn2+ present.

But could be mixture of Fe3+ and Mn2+ where Fe3+ not giving complex due to low concentration? However Fe3+ complex with SCN is very sensitive; should appear red even at low conc. So likely absent.

Thus answer: Mn2+.

Group III cations list: Fe3+, Al3+, Cr3+, Mn2+, Zn2+, Pb2+, Cu2+, Ni2+, Co2+. So we output "Mn2+".
